text:
ingrid: Heads-up — Observed repeated OTLP exporter queue evictions for Tempo during last deploy. Several spans dropped. Anyone else seeing this?

devon: Yup saw traces missing from Tempo for ~2min at 03:12 UTC. Exporter logs show "queue full, drop span".

marta: Can you paste the logs you saw?

ingrid: Pasted snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T03:12:10Z exporter/tempo info queue_size=65536 dropped=1200 err="queue full"
2026-03-15T03:12:11Z exporter/tempo warn retrying batch id=0x7fa5 attempts=1
```

ryan: Are we running tail-based sampling? We only do tail sampling in the collector path, services are emitting everything. If bursts hit the collector, downstream exporters will choke.

alex: Config looks on the conservative side. Current OTLP batch processor in prod: 
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.internal:4317
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 512
    timeout: 10s
service:
  telemetry:
    metrics_level: basic
```

devon: We also have per-tenant ingress quotas upstream — bursts sometimes bypass the soft quota window and flood exporters.

marta: Two paths: (A) exporter-level backpressure+honor Retry-After, with exponential backoff + jitter; (B) local bounded queue with eviction policy that prefers keeping high-value spans and drops noisy ones first. Also consider pre-export sampling for known noisy routes.

ingrid: Sketch of a tenant-aware eviction policy we discussed: 
```yaml
queue:
  max_items: 100000
  eviction_policy: priority_per_tenant
  priority_rules:
    - match: "http.status_code=2xx"
      score: -10
    - match: "span.kind=internal"
      score: -5
    - match: "env=prod"
      score: 10
    - match: "tenant_tier=premium"
      score: 20
```

ryan: Tenant-aware eviction is good. We need O(1) scoring code — avoid slow regex on insert. Use indexed attribute checks for tenant_id, env, http.status.

alex: Also: we must emit metrics for observability: `exporter.queue_depth`, `exporter.evicted_spans_by_tenant`, `exporter.retry_rate`. Console dashboards should have per-tenant heatmaps so SRE/product can correlate drops to customers.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: collector v0.72.3 -> prod on 2026-03-18T08:00:00Z.

marta: One more angle — retention mismatch. If Tempo TTL < our aggregator retention, users will see disappeared traces even if we exported them. We need retention headers or a retention sync policy.

devon: For Datadog exporter we saw 429s with `Retry-After`. We should add handler that: (1) honors Retry-After, (2) routes excess traffic to a fallback path (Splunk blob or archive), (3) marks spans as partial-export so UI can surface incompleteness.

ingrid: Action items: 
- [Marta] design eviction policy + O(1) scoring lib + test plan (due: 2026-03-19)
- [Devon] implement Retry-After honoring + split-export prototype (due: 2026-03-22)
- [Alex] dashboard mockups: queue depth, evictions, per-tenant drop rate (due: 2026-03-20)
- [Ryan] sync with Tempo team about retention windows and partial ingest (due: 2026-03-21)

alex: +1 :thumbsup:

ryan: I'll ping Tempo infra to confirm acceptable retention and any per-tenant TTL headers.

marta: I'll post an RFC with algorithm notes and microbench numbers tomorrow.

devon: I'll prototype the Retry-After handler and add a test that simulates 429 + Retry-After 10s.

ingrid: thanks all — keeping this thread as the decision log. If you add commits, reference `telemetry/exporter-eviction` branch. :raised_hands:
